content: 1. Almotriptan: The level or effect of almotriptan may be reduced due to alterations in hepatic or intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 2. Alpelisib and Etravirine: Alpelisib can decrease the level or effect of etravirine by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Etravirine and Alprazolam: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of alprazolam by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 4. Amiodarone and Etravirine: Amiodarone can increase the level or effect of etravirine by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 5. Etravirine and Amitriptyline: Etravirine may increase the level or effect of amitriptyline by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 6. Amobarbital and Etravirine: Amobarbital can reduce the level or effect of etravirine by influencing CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 7. Apalutamide and Etravirine: Apalutamide may decrease the level or effect of etravirine by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. When coadministered with CYP2C9 substrates, evaluate for potential loss of therapeutic effect. 8. Aprepitant and Etravirine: Aprepitant can increase the level or effect of etravirine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine may reduce the level or effect of aprepitant. Use caution and monitor the patient. 9. Etravirine and Aripiprazole: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of aripiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 10. Armodafinil and Etravirine: Armodafinil can both increase and decrease the level or effect of etravirine by influencing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Use caution and monitor the patient. 11. Atazanavir and Etravirine: Atazanavir may increase the level or effect of etravirine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 12. Etravirine and Atogepant: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The recommended atogepant dosage with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is 30 mg or 60 mg once daily. 13. Etravirine and Atorvastatin: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of atorvastatin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 14. Etravirine and Avanafil: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of avanafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. For patients with erectile dysfunction, carefully monitor response due to potential reduced effectiveness. 15. Etravirine and Avapritinib: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of avapritinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 16. Etravirine and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 17. Etravirine and Belumosudil: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of belumosudil by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A inducers. 18. Belzutifan and Etravirine: Belzutifan may reduce the level or effect of etravirine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the substrate dose as per prescribing information. 19. Etravirine and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Exercise caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers coadministered with benzhydrocodone, as plasma hydrocodone concentrations may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 20. Etravirine and Betrixaban: Etravirine increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 21. Etravirine and Bexarotene: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of bexarotene by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 22. Bortezomib and Etravirine: Bortezomib may increase the level or effect of etravirine by altering CYP2C19 metabolism, while etravirine may reduce the level or effect of bortezomib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 23. Bosentan and Etravirine: Bosentan may reduce the level or effect of etravirine by influencing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Etravirine and Brexpiprazole: Etravirine may decrease the level or effect of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 25. Etravirine and Bromocriptine: Etravirine may reduce the level or effect of bromocriptine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient.
